title: Spare parts inventory with reorder points for a packaging line
summary: A living spare-parts list for a fictional packaging line with on-hand counts, reorder points, and who owns the buy.

blocks.title: Spares that match the line's failure modes
blocks.body: Fictional Line P3 (flow wrapper + case erector) keeps a small crib of parts that actually stop the line when missing. Reorder points below are examples — tune to your lead times.

blocks.title: Operating policy
blocks.body: If on-hand ≤ reorder point, create a PO the same shift. Critical parts (marked) escalate to the planner within an hour if the PO cannot place.

blocks.heading: Line P3 spare crib (example)
blocks.caption: Example SKUs and counts for a teaching line — not a vendor catalog.

blocks.heading: How these reorder points were set (method)
items: List parts that stopped Line P3 in the last year (historian + WO tags).
For each, note supplier lead time and how many failures occur before a spare arrives.
Reorder point ≈ expected use during lead time + a small buffer for weekends.
Review quarterly — a part that never moves may not deserve crib space.

columns.name: Technician
columns.detail: Draws parts with a scan or tag; notes if bin hits reorder.

columns.name: Planner / crib owner
columns.detail: Places POs; adjusts reorder points; kills zombie SKUs.

columns.name: Supervisor
columns.detail: Escalates critical stockouts that threaten the shift.

items.label: Scan or count critical bins that moved today
Create PO for anything ≤ reorder point
Flag open critical POs older than lead time
items.detail: Chase suppliers before the line does.

items.label: Return unused draws
items.detail: Phantom stockouts often start as parts in a toolbox.

items.title: Knife blade drawn
items.detail: On hand 2→1; already at reorder — PO placed.

items.title: Two photoeyes fail same day
items.detail: On hand 4→2; hits reorder; PO for +4.

items.title: Belt still at 1
items.detail: Critical at reorder floor — confirm PO status before weekend.

blocks.heading: Reorder check
blocks.prompt: Ice-cube relays show on hand 4 and reorder at 4. What should happen?
options: Place a PO this shift per policy (≤ reorder point)
blocks.explanation: Policy uses ≤ reorder point. Sitting on the line is already late enough.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct — order at the floor, not after a stockout.

blocks.heading: Keep the crib honest
blocks.body: Inventory is an operating system. Counts without reorder action are just a museum of almost-useful plastic bins.
